newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- OCT 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- OCT 11.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
KATHIMERINI

--Timidity and vagueness: the government's policy statements reveal discrepancy between painful conclusions about how far Greece is from its European partners and painless statements on how to breach the gap.
--Sharp retort from Town Planning and Public Works Minister Costas Laliotis on court ruling on transfer of building restrictions. Court cannot legislate or hinder economic activity, he says.
ELEFTHEROTYPIA

--Simitis rings the alarm bells and promises protection for low income earners, emphasis on a 'social state' and for the affluent to pay more. 'Political costs' not a factor as he appeals to opposition parties for consensus.
--There will be no dialogue with Turkey if it does not see reason, the prime minister says. Greece's sovereignty and territorial integrity are not up for questioning or talks, he says.

--The toll of the 'undeclared war' in the Aegean. The Greek Air Force needs 200 million drachmas a week to police the Aegean while the Navy needs 230 million a month to patrol.The bill for 21 years is 10 trillion drachmas and six dead Greeks and Turks.
--Procedures to give three Turkish soldiers political asylum begin, following a storm of reaction to their court-ordered deportation.
TA NEA
--Smaller parties call for equal treatment on the first day of the three-day Parliamentary debate.
--Government announces a four-year term of difficulties in the economic and national sector.

--In foreign policy, no dialogue with Turkey on sovereign rights, a strong armed forces with modernised weapons systems, resolution of Cyprus issue and a Cyprus accession to EU a first priority, the name of the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia to be resolved in UN negotiations.

--In public administration, systematic evaluation of services and public servants, increased computerisation in all sectors, meritocratic appointments, offensive on corruption in public sector, decentralisation of state administration.
--In economy, increases above inflation, abolition of tax breaks increasing social inequality, strict adherence to convergence programme, Greece to join EMU by 2000, creation of 180,000 new jobs.

--In social welfare, changes to security system, unified principles and criteria for health services, low pensions to be pegged to cost of living, farmers' pension fund to become a major fund, expansion of 'family doctors' and qualitative upgrading of health system.
ETHNOS
--The last chance for Greece to succeed, Simitis says as he spells out his six axes for a strong Greece.

--The truth about Dimitra Liani-Papandreou (the widow of ruling party PASOK founder and former prime minister George Papandreou) and Costas Spyropoulos (the partner of the late Aliki Vouyiouklaki, a popular Greek actress) - what the gardener saw.
ELEFTHEROS TYPOS

--The end of the national higher school certificate. The prime minister pulls the rug out from under George Papandreou, former education minister, suspending the application of a new high school education system to the next century.
--Simitis's programme: 82 'Ifs' and 27 'Shoulds'. The only clear message: austerity continues.Taxes: the haves and have nots will pay.
--Main opposition leader Miltiades Evert: Never have we sat for so long to hear so little.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
